name: utmp_parse
description: Parse the binary login records wtmp, btmp, utmp and lastlog, in the layouts it names: glibc `struct utmp` (384-byte records) and `struct lastlog` (292 or 296 bytes, indexed by UID). Each record has its type, user, line, source host and address (raw bytes beside it), PID, session, ut_exit (exit_termination, exit_status) and time, and where it sits in the file: record index and byte offset, or UID slot. The answer names the layout and byte order it used and how it chose: a utmp byte order from the records' ut_type (the order in which more non-empty records have a type of 1-9, over a sample; `undetermined` where every record is empty, refused as ambiguous where both orders fit), and the file refused as not 384-byte records where fewer than 80% of its non-empty records have such a type (another C library's record size reads that way; layout: utmp-384 or a byte_order reads it anyway, and the answer then says all_records_read is false), a lastlog layout from the file size where only one width divides it or, where both do, from whether every non-empty slot's line and host are NUL-padded strings (refused as ambiguous where nothing tells them apart: pass layout; byte_order for lastlog is the little-endian default, said to be untested). Raw seconds and microseconds are kept, a tv_usec outside 0..999999 gives no time and says so, and nothing is reduced to look plausible; a short tail is named with its offset and size. A file whose name starts with `lastlog` (lastlog.1 too) is read as lastlog. A sparse lastlog is read skipping holes (holes_skipped says whether they were) within max_slots and max_seconds, with next_uid to resume and uids to read only named slots; a utmp file is read within max_seconds, with stopped_at_record and start_record to resume. passwd (lastlog only) names the accounts and the answer says which file it read and how many UIDs it mapped; without it no account is named. The arguments of the other kind (uids, start_uid, max_slots, passwd for utmp; start_record, user_is_typed for lastlog) are refused, not ignored. It does not read wtmpdb or lastlog2 (SQLite: refused, pointing at sqlite_query), another C library's record sizes or a 64-bit utmp time field (refused by the type check above, not read as 384-byte records), or a record nobody wrote: a missing record is not a login that did not happen, and a USER_PROCESS without a later DEAD_PROCESS is not shown to be open. SENSITIVE: btmp holds failed logins, and its user field is what was typed, which can be a password typed into the wrong field: in a file named btmp (or with user_is_typed: true) the answer carries only the name's length (user_bytes), and a `user` filter matches only in a job. write_text: true (refused outside a job) writes it to $OUT/utmp-text.jsonl, mode 0600; preview_text: true (refused outside a job) puts it in the answer; run it as a job with secret_output: true. wtmp and utmp name accounts that logged in, and their user stays in the answer. Every answer carries `status` (complete, partial or failed) and `status_basis`, the pair the recipes' coverage.json carries: all_records_read stays beside it.

path.description: A wtmp, btmp, utmp or lastlog file (a link is refused; a SQLite file is refused with a pointer)

types.description: Keep only these record types, e.g. ["USER_PROCESS","BOOT_TIME"]; counts by type and boots are always over every record

user.description: Case-insensitive regex over the user name (a lastlog slot: the name from passwd). Over a typed name (btmp, or user_is_typed) it matches only in a job, and the answer says filter_touched_withheld_text

format.description: Force utmp or lastlog; otherwise lastlog is chosen by a file name that starts with 'lastlog'

layout.description: auto (default), utmp-384, lastlog-292 or lastlog-296. Name it where the answer says the lastlog layout is ambiguous

byte_order.description: auto (default: a utmp file's order is decided from its records), little or big

passwd.description: lastlog only: a passwd file of the evidence (a regular file), used to map UID slots to account names; the answer names it and how many UIDs it mapped

uids.description: lastlog only: read just the slots of these UIDs (a sparse file is not walked); the answer says its scope is the selected UIDs

start_uid.description: lastlog only: the first UID of the walk (default 0); next_uid in an earlier answer resumes it

max_slots.description: lastlog only: how many UID slots to cover in this call (holes count); the answer's next_uid says where the rest begins

max_seconds.description: The time to spend (default 30, at most 45): a utmp file is read record by record and a lastlog walked slot by slot; what is left is named (stopped_at_record, next_uid) and the answer is partial

limit.description: Records shown inline (default 200); all are counted and, when there are more, the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in pages.records.all_results

start_record.description: utmp only: the first record to read (default 0); stopped_at_record in an earlier answer resumes it

user_is_typed.description: utmp only: auto (default: a file named btmp holds typed names), true or false. A typed name is withheld from the answer

write_text.description: Write each record's user (a typed name) beside its locator to $OUT/utmp-text.jsonl (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; a file already there is refused

preview_text.description: Put a typed name in the answer's records (default false). Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true
